note: Known cross-platform divergences on fixtures/visual-test.json, seeded from a live three-platform run (327 pairs, 23 failing at SSIM<0.95 || dpx>2%). A LEDGER, not a tolerance: each line names one divergence, why it is believed benign or why it is a bug, who owns it, and when it must be re-reviewed. Deleting a line is how a fix gets recorded. READ THIS: 6 of these entries are REAL SIZE BUGS surfaced for the first time by the magenta pad sentinel - before that fix a short render was padded with the capture background and scored a perfect diff. They carry a short expiry because they need fixing, not excusing. Of the remainder, almost all fail on SSIM alone with dpx well under the 2% budget and deltaE95 = 0.00 - the colours are exact and SSIM is scoring curve/transform anti-aliasing. That is evidence about the METRIC, not the runtimes, and most of those lines should evaporate when the gate moves off SSIM. ALSO measured on composition-test.json (2026-08-26): pixelmatch at threshold 0.25 reported pixelMismatchedPct 0.00 for 037_Nested_OpacityGroup while 36.63% of pixels differ by up to 80 per channel. Its YIQ budget is 0.25*35215 = 8803.8, and a PURE LIGHTNESS shift must exceed 132/255 to be counted — so black (0,0,0) vs mid-grey (130,130,130) is reported as identical. The 2% pixel gate therefore cannot fire on any uniform lightness error smaller than half the dynamic range. Only SSIM (0.9355) and deltaE95 (20.94) caught this row.

expectations.reason: REAL BUG (Android) — a child carrying mix-blend-mode is painted at (width - left) x (height - top) instead of its authored size. Measured on all four blend modes: authored 140x50 at left:40 top:20, Android paints 100x30; the ORIGIN is correct (x56,y36) so only the extent is wrong. Blend-specific: in Blend_Normal_OverGradient_Control Android paints the full 140x50. The blend maths itself is right - sampled multiply results match child*backdrop/255 to within rounding inside the painted region on all three platforms. iOS and web agree with each other exactly here.

REAL BUG — backdrop-filter: blur() is silently dropped on ANDROID too, not just iOS. Proven by the control: Android renders Backdrop_Blur_OverStripes 0 px different from Backdrop_None_OverStripes_Control while web differs by 8000 px. saturate(4) IS implemented on Android (4000 px vs its control), so the gap is specifically blur(). Both natives drop it, which is why iOS-Android does NOT diverge on this row - they agree on the wrong answer. That is the correlated-failure mode a three-way comparison cannot detect on its own.

REAL BUG — backdrop-filter: blur() is SILENTLY DROPPED on iOS. Proven by the paired control, not inferred: iOS renders Backdrop_Blur_OverStripes pixel-identical to Backdrop_None_OverStripes_Control (0 px difference) while web differs by 8000 px. backdrop-filter: saturate(4) IS implemented on iOS (4000 px vs its control), so the gap is specifically blur(). This is why visual-test.json's Glass_Effect has always passed: it blurs a UNIFORM field, where the correct result and the dropped result are the same image.

REAL BUG (iOS) — iOS applies parent opacity per child instead of compositing the subtree as a group; Android agrees with web here, so iOS is the lone outlier. Arithmetic: blue child #2980b9 = (41,128,185) over page (26,26,46) - web/Android give (33,77,116) = 0.5*child + 0.5*page (group, correct); iOS gives (90,134,168) = 0.5*child + 0.5*(140,140,151), the child faded individually over the already-faded parent. Max per-channel divergence 80.

REAL BUG — iOS applies parent opacity PER CHILD instead of compositing the subtree as a group. css-color-4: opacity on an element creates a stacking context and the whole subtree is rendered as a group, then composited once. The arithmetic pins it exactly: for the blue child #2980b9 = (41,128,185) over page background (26,26,46), web gives (33,77,116) = 0.5*child + 0.5*page (group-composited, CORRECT); iOS gives (90,134,168) = 0.5*child + 0.5*(140,140,151), i.e. the child faded individually over the already-faded parent background. Max per-channel divergence 80. Also note pixelmatch reports pixelMismatchedPct 0.00 here while 36.63%% of pixels actually differ — see the metric note below.
